messages:
customer-jd: Hey - customers on our app are seeing partial/trimmed messages from the Redwood streaming chat endpoint. The stream opens and sends a few chunks, then stops with no closing event. No HTTP 500, connection stays ESTABLISHED on client side for ~30s then closes. Happening across SSE and websocket clients. Sample request IDs: r-9f3a2b7c, r-9f3a2b9d, r-9f3a2ba1.

jess (Support): Sorry about that — we'll triage. Can you confirm which API path you're hitting (v1/chat vs v1/streams), sample curl you used, and whether there's a proxy or CDN in front of the client? Also paste one of the raw request IDs and approximate client timestamps.

customer-jd: It's v1/chat with streaming=true. Behind a CDN (FastEdge) + internal proxy. One example: r-9f3a2b9d, client time 2026-03-17T15:12:03Z. We can reproduce by hitting our staging behind same stack.

jess (Support): Thanks. Two quick asks while we dig: 1) run a direct curl from a host with no CDN in between and post output, 2) capture logs from the proxy for the same request ID, and 3) a small reproducible curl that we can run from our side.

omar (SRE): Also include `ngrep -W byline port 443` or a tcpdump pcap if possible. If it's a buffering issue the TCP-level trace will show large final packet sizes or stalled ACKs.

maria (Eng Runtime): Suspect client-side buffering or connection-level pauses; we've seen proxies coalesce SSE frames. If you can reproduce with plain curl, include the raw bytes. Here's a small curl reproducer we use for SSE that avoids libcurl buffering:

```bash
export KEY=REDACTED
echo '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"stream test"}],"stream":true}' > /tmp/payload.json
curl -v -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/chat -d @/tmp/payload.json --max-time 120
```

maria (Eng Runtime): Note the `-N`/`--no-buffer` flag to disable curl's buffering. If curl still shows truncation but the server logs show full tokens, it's likely client/CDN buffering.

customer-jd: Ran that from a host without CDN and it still truncated once. Attached a small paste of the stdout: 

```
> POST /v1/chat HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.com
> Authorization: Bearer ****
> Accept: text/event-stream

data: {"id":"r-9f3a2b9d","chunk":"It looks like we're almost done with the response, finishing thought about deployment..."}
data: {"id":"r-9f3a2b9d","chunk":" — but then it just stops"}

# connection hangs for ~30s then closes, no `event: done`
```

jess (Support): Good capture. Can you also get the server-side request logs? We need the redwood request log lines for r-9f3a2b9d (ingress -> runtime -> stream-fanout). If you can't, we can pull them if you grant debug bundle access.

customer-jd: I can share the app logs and the proxy logs. How do we create the debug bundle?

ops-bot: To collect a debug bundle run: `curl -X POST "https://console.redwood.com/debug-bundles" -H "Authorization: Bearer <support-token>" -d '{"request_ids":["r-9f3a2b9d"],"include_pcap":true}'` — this will give a signed upload link.

omar (SRE): When you upload the pcap please ensure it contains the TLS handshake and the entire connection. If you can't share TLS keys, a metadata pcap is fine but full packet bytes help. Also include proxy config (nginx/fastedge) and any keepalive/read timeout settings.

maria (Eng Runtime): If you can re-run with `curl --no-buffer -H "Connection: keep-alive" -H "Accept: text/event-stream"` and post both the full raw output and our server request logs for r-9f3a2b9d (we'll look for incomplete write syscall or worker restart). If possible, also paste the runtime debug trace snippet we recently added: `runtime:stream:write:duration` entries around that req id.

customer-jd: OK I'll collect and upload. One more data point: their mobile client (WebView) shows output but last sentence is missing — makes me lean client buffering. Anything to toggle on our side quickly?

maria (Eng Runtime): For WebView clients, ensure `text/event-stream` is not being reinterpreted by the WebView. Also try disabling response-splitting middleware and lowering proxy `proxy_buffer_size` to avoid aggregation. Quick test: set `proxy_buffering off;` in nginx for the stream endpoint and see if that eliminates the aggregation.

jess (Support): Plan: 1) customer uploads debug bundle + pcap + proxy logs, 2) SRE inspects tcp/tcpdump for stalls, 3) Eng Runtime looks at server write traces and runtime errors, 4) we coordinate a small canary test with `proxy_buffering off`. We'll update this thread with findings. :thumbsup:

customer-jd: Uploading bundle now — link incoming in a minute. Thanks all.

ops-bot: Debug bundle uploaded: https://console.redwood.com/signed-upload/abc123 (expires in 24h)

omar (SRE): Got it, pulling pcap. If I see retransmits or zero-window events I'll post a tcpdump excerpt.

maria (Eng Runtime): Also adding a short runtime patch to add an extra flush call after final chunk for the session if we detect a streaming client flag; we'll test in staging and report back.

jess (Support): Thanks team. Customer, we'll follow up here once we have packet analysis and runtime traces.

customer-jd: Appreciate it — will watch the thread.
